translations.text: Then Herod called the three astrologers to a private conference, and eagerly asked them at what time the star had first appeared to them, and sent them to Bethlehem,
They saw the star and rejoiced greatly. Then they went in and found the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they worshipped him.
Now historians say that meanwhile Herod was accused before the Roman emperor, who at that time ruled the whole world.
Then he went to Rome at the emperor's command, so that he might clear himself, if he could.
Then he cleared himself very cunningly, being so very eloquent that the emperor sent him back to the Jewish kingdom with greater honour.
When he came home, he remembered what he had earlier intended concerning the child, and saw that he had been deceived by the astrologers, and he became greatly enraged.
Then he called the astrologers to a private conference, and eagerly asked them at what time they had first seen the star, because he feared, as indeed happened, that they would not come back to him.
but it would have been too soon if he had been killed then in the cradle, as though his coming would then have been hidden from mankind;
They are called the flowers of the martyrs, because they were like flowers springing up in the midst of the cold of unbelief, withered as it were by the frost of persecution.
Blessed are the wombs that bore them, and the breasts that suckled such ones.
They were killed while small and without understanding, but they will arise at the common judgement with full stature and heavenly wisdom.
Rachel was the name of the wife of Jacob the patriarch, and she signified God's Church, which weeps for her spiritual children;

but she will not be comforted in such a way that they should return again to worldly struggle, those who once overcame the world through a victorious death and escaped its miseries, to be crowned with glory with Christ.

Truly the impious Herod did not enjoy his kingdom with long-lasting prosperity, but without delay divine vengeance came upon him, which destroyed him with manifold misery, and also showed in what torments he must suffer eternally after his death.
An unspeakable disease seized him; his body burned outwardly with a lingering fever, and he was likewise all burned up within, and burst apart.
He had a great desire for food, yet he could not satisfy his greed with any amount of eating. He shook with fever, and wheezed dreadfully, and drew anguished sighs, so that he could hardly breathe.
Dropsy overcame him below the girdle, to such an extent that his genitals swarmed with worms, and stinking poison flowed continually from his swollen feet.
Unbearable itching overcame his whole body, and an incredible swelling afflicted his bowels.
A stinking vapour came from his mouth, so that hardly any physician could come near him. He killed many of the physicians, saying that they could heal him and would not.
He was tormented by constant sleeplessness, so that he spent whole wakeful nights without sleep; and if he dozed a little, nightly phantoms at once tormented him, so that sleep became hateful to him.
When he longed intensely for his life, he ordered himself to be carried across the river Jordan, to where there were hot baths, which were said to be healing for sick bodies.
Then it also seemed good to his physicians that they should bathe him in warm oil.
But when he was brought into this bathing, his body went completely limp, so that his eyes turned like those of dying men, and he lay speechless and senseless.
Afterwards, when he came back, he ordered himself to be carried to the city of Jericho.
When he despaired of his life, he summoned to him all the Jewish elders from every city and ordered them to be shut up in prison, and he called to him his sister Salome and her husband Alexander,
and said, "I know that this Jewish people will greatly rejoice at my death; but I can have honourable funeral rites from a mourning multitude, if you will obey my commands.
"As soon as I die, kill all these Jewish elders whom I have shut up in prison; then their kinsmen, who would rejoice at my death, will be forced into mourning."
He then appointed his soldiers for the slaughter and ordered each of them to be given fifty shillings as payment, so that they would not hold back their hands from the bloodshed.
When he was tormented with immense anguish, he ordered his own son Antipater to be wickedly killed, in addition to the two whom he had killed before.
At last, when he felt his death approaching, he ordered his knife to be handed to him to pare an apple, and he stabbed himself violently, so that it quivered in him.
Such was the death of Herod, who wickedly plotted against the coming of the heavenly prince, and impiously killed the innocent little children of the same age as him.
Then, after Herod's death, God's angel appeared to Joseph in dreams in the land of Egypt, saying: "Arise, and take the child and his mother together, and go back to the land of Israel;
for truly those who plotted against the child's life are dead." Then he arose, as the angel had commanded him, and brought the child with the mother to the land of Israel.
Then Joseph learned that Archelaus reigned in the land of Judea after his father Herod, and he did not dare to come near him.
Then he was again admonished in a dream that he should turn aside to Galilee, because that region was not so very near to the king, though it was in his kingdom.
The child then lived in the town called Nazareth, so that the prophecy might be fulfilled which said that he would be called a Nazarene.
The angel said to Joseph: "Those who plotted against the child's life are dead."
With that word he showed that more of the Jewish elders had plotted Christ's death; but it befell them very justly that they all perished together with their impious lord.
We will not draw out this story any longer, lest it seem tedious to you; but ask for intercession for yourselves from these innocent martyrs.
They are the ones who follow Christ in white garments wherever he goes; and they stand before his throne without any stain,
having their palm branches in their hands, and they sing the new song of praise in honour of the Almighty, who lives and reigns for ever without end. Amen.
